original_card.question: Can one small, precisely scoped interface lemma be formalized with its actual hypotheses?
methods: Formalize a missing boundary lemma identified by the selected review.
Audit a formal theorem-to-certificate binding independently.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State the exact formalized proposition and remaining assumptions; avoid duplicate arithmetic formalizations already present.

first_step.inspect: Read the exact hypotheses in the hyperplane-end proof and distinguish Lean theorems from finite supplier assumptions.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: State one missing boundary lemma in full before starting a proof-assistant build.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A missing interface proof can reduce the conditional gap even if it does not change kappa.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one formal lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding.
scope_change_triggers: Formalizing already-covered arithmetic and claiming the full multiplication theorem.

actual_scope: Separately authored audit of PR1560's written Theorem 1 (structural zero exclusion) and Corollary 2 (gauge form) at head eb9f6f15, and of the theorem-to-certificate binding used by PR1616 (7b3e4624) and PR1650 (d960f8a2): (1) a step-by-step written audit over an arbitrary characteristic-zero field; (2) an exact stdlib check, written from the prose only, of the finite E8 facts the proof uses implicitly, at every one of the 2025 frames as pivot; (3) a reading of PR1616/PR1650's criterion code against the stated hypotheses, plus a cross-check of PR1650's verdicts against a second implementation with different exact methods.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for one interface lemma or one theorem-to-certificate binding. PR1560's theorem is the single unreviewed written step behind the P107, P106 and P105 rigidity results of PR1616/PR1650, which apply it at hundreds of pivots other than the one PR1560's checker covers; PR1560 states no independent human review, and PR1650 cites rather than re-derives it. This is an audit, not a proof-assistant formalization.
bottleneck_link: Side result for the complex-decoder lower-bound line (no kappa). It provides a separately authored written audit (not a formal proof) of one unreviewed proof obligation under the PR968 copy floors claimed at P107-P105 through #1212 section 8.
stop_rule: Stop at a written audit plus exact checks of every finite fact the proof uses; any genuine gap is reported as a FINDING instead of being patched silently.
evidence: Corroborated, no gap in Theorem 1 or Corollary 2 (one expository omission in Corollary 2 filled in the README). verify.py: implicit finite facts E1-E8 hold at all 2025 pivot frames (about 50 s). binding_crosscheck.py: PR1650's criterion agrees with a second implementation on every sampled case (see README).
author: Josie Elliston (with Claude Opus 5.5)
ai_assistance: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic) via Claude Code wrote the audit, both scripts and the README under Josie Elliston's account; a Codex read-only review was requested.
